Is It Safe to Compress Photos and ID Images Online?

By Kamlesh Mohabe, Software Engineer · Published 2026-10-04

How to judge whether an online image tool is safe for personal photos: local processing versus uploads, what to check, and what you should still do yourself.

Question: Where does my photo go?

It depends on the tool. Some compressors upload your image to a server, process it there and send a result back. Others process it on your own device in the browser. The second kind is generally lower risk for personal photos, because the image never needs to leave your device for compression.

Question: How does ImageTo20KB work?

The compression uses the Canvas feature of your browser. Your file is read, decoded, resized and re-encoded on your device. There is no upload step for compression, and no image-processing service is called. The site is static, so there is no server-side storage of your images. You can read the details on the how it works and privacy pages.

Question: How can I check a tool’s claims?

Read its privacy policy, and look for specific statements about where processing happens. A technical user can open the browser’s network panel while compressing and see whether the image is sent anywhere. Be wary of tools that require an account, ask for unnecessary permissions, or show a lot of advertising.

Question: What risks remain even with local processing?

Downloaded files stay on your device, so shared or public computers are a risk. Browser extensions can read page content. Malware on your device is outside any website’s control. And a website can change over time, so check the policy again if you are handling something sensitive.

Question: Should I process Aadhaar, PAN or passport images?

Only do it when you must, such as for a form that requires it, and only on your own device. Avoid sending such images by email or messaging apps. Delete copies you no longer need. Do not claim any tool is perfectly safe, including ours.

Good habits

Use your own device. Keep the browser updated. Close the tab when finished. Delete downloaded files you no longer need. Prefer tools that say where processing happens and that list a contact for questions.

What we promise and what we do not

We describe how the tool works as accurately as we can. We do not promise absolute security. If you find a problem, email us at the address on the contact page.

What to look for in a privacy policy

A useful policy says plainly whether images are uploaded, whether they are stored and for how long, what data the site collects about visitors, which third parties receive it, and how to contact the owner. Vague promises such as "we take privacy seriously" without details are not enough. Check the date of the last update, and be cautious if a tool asks you to create an account just to resize one picture. Our own policy is on the privacy page, including the parts that depend on our hosting provider.

It is also worth noticing what a tool does not ask for. A compressor that only needs a file does not need your phone number, your location, your contacts or access to your camera roll beyond the file you choose. If a site requests more, ask why before you continue.
